city.Port Moresby.flag: a diagonal split — a bird of paradise on red, the Southern Cross on black
city.Reykjavik.description: Iceland's governmental assembly, the Althing, is the world's oldest surviving parliament.
city.Rio de Janeiro.description: Brazil's capital is Brasilia, an entirely new city recently built in the interior of the country.
city.Rio de Janeiro.greeting: In Portuguese, a casual hi is “Oi” (oy).
city.Rio de Janeiro.flag: green with a yellow diamond and a blue globe crossed by a starry band
city.Rome.description: During the Renaissance, Italy was divided into numerous city-states which were vital centers of art, science and learning.
city.Rome.greeting: In Italian, a casual hi is “Ciao” (chow).
city.Rome.flag: three bands of green, white and red
city.San Marino.description: Postage stamps and tourism are San Marino's largest industries. This tiny country's full name is Most Serene Republic of San Marino.
city.San Marino.greeting: In Italian, people greet you with “Buongiorno” (bwohn-JOR-noh) — it means “good day.”
city.San Marino.flag: white above light blue with a shield of three towers
city.Singapore.description: The nation of Singapore, located near the equator in Southeast Asia, consists of one large island plus 40 smaller islands.
city.Singapore.landmark: the tip of the Malay Peninsula
city.Singapore.greeting: In Malay, “Apa khabar?” (AH-pah KAH-bar) means “how are you?”.
city.Singapore.flag: red above white with a white crescent moon and five stars
city.Sydney.description: An island continent, Australia is nearly as large as the United States but has only about one-twelfth the population.
city.Sydney.greeting: In Australia, a classic hello is “G’day” (guh-DAY).
city.Sydney.flag: blue with a Union Jack and the white stars of the Southern Cross
city.Tokyo.description: Tokyo, with a population of about 14 million people, is the capital and largest city in Japan.
city.Tokyo.flag: white with a large red circle in the center
